create.name: Howard Cohn
create.bio:
Howard Cohn, known to students as Howie, has practised meditation since 1972 and has led vipassana retreats in the United States and abroad since 1985. Alongside the Theravada insight tradition he has studied Zen, Dzogchen and Advaita Vedanta with Asian and Western teachers, with a strong influence from the Indian teacher H. W. L. Poonja. He has long taught at Spirit Rock Meditation Center in California, and was one of the first members of its council of teachers.

In 1990 he founded Mission Dharma, a sitting group in San Francisco's Mission District that he still leads. It now meets on Tuesday evenings on Zoom for a period of meditation, questions and a talk, offered on a donation basis, and many of his talks are posted on the group's YouTube channel. His teaching is warm and often humorous, and returns again and again to resting in awareness and rediscovering a freedom that is already present. He also leads silent retreats several times a year and offers one-to-one practice interviews and mentoring. His book Invitation to Meditation, with a foreword by Jack Kornfield, is a short guide for beginners that leads readers into practice as they read.

books.title: Invitation to Meditation: How to Find Peace Wherever You Are
books.author: Howard Cohn
books.description: A short, gentle introduction for newcomers, with a foreword by Jack Kornfield. Each page is written so that the reader starts practising while reading, building a habit of returning to the present moment.

free_resources.title: Mission Dharma Tuesday Night Sangha
free_resources.description: A weekly evening gathering on Zoom, led most weeks by Howie, with forty minutes of meditation followed by questions and a dharma talk. Offered by donation, with no one turned away.

free_resources.title: Mission Dharma Talk Archive
free_resources.description: Recorded Tuesday night talks by Howie and guest teachers, listed by date and free to download. Newer talks appear on the group's YouTube channel.
